title: Canvas
definition: The `<canvas>` element is used to draw graphics on a web page via JavaScript. It is a resolution-dependent bitmap canvas.
simpleExplanation: HTML creates a blank box. JavaScript grabs a digital paintbrush and actually draws lines, circles, text, or entire video games inside that box pixel by pixel.
realWorldExample: Browser-based video games (like Flappy Bird clones), interactive charts (Chart.js), or signature pads where users draw their signature with a mouse.

basic: Does the `<canvas>` tag draw graphics by itself?
intermediate: What is the difference between Canvas and SVG?

answers.question: Draw by itself?
answers.answer: No. The `<canvas>` tag is just an empty container. You MUST use JavaScript to draw anything on it.

answers.question: Canvas vs SVG?
answers.answer: Canvas is pixel-based (bitmap). If you zoom in, it gets blurry. It's great for games with thousands of moving objects. SVG is math-based (vector). It never loses quality when zoomed, and each shape is a real DOM element you can target with CSS.
